evidence: Image fill 0x0062AB10-0x0062AB71: loads field_5B0_/field_5AC_/field_5A0_/field_59C_ into eax/edx/esi/edi, stores [ecx+0x58C]/[ecx+0x590]/[ecx+0x594]/[ecx+0x598], then reloads mov eax,[ecx+0x5A0]; mov edx,[ecx+0x59C]; mov eax,[ecx+0x5B0]; mov edx,[ecx+0x5AC] to push the Buffer::fill (0x005D8240) arguments.

Deck build/recovery/decks/fill-rect-v1.out: the direct-scalar and anonymous-union-array candidates boundary-fail at 80 bytes with no reload block, while every pointer-store candidate reaches the recorded 98-byte extent with the four member reloads - the union-array variant refutes the hypothesis that array-member stores invalidate the load cache.

decode_fli_copy's prologue 0x0062ABB0-0x0062ABE5 and decode_black_trans's body repeat the identical load/store/reload shape with esi=this, tying the same spelling to the whole family, including decode_chunk's two inline type-0xD arms.

Post-switch check build/recovery/decks/check-after-rect-plain.out (26 compile attempts, both flag sets): fill and decode_black_trans fail with differing offsets confined to 26-49 - the store/add region - with loads and reloads byte-exact; no previously passing function regressed (counts unchanged at 6 pass / 12 fail / 6 unknown).
payload.hypothesis: The Flic dirty-rectangle store block (four stores to field_58C_-field_598_ feeding a Buffer call) reproduces the image's per-use member reloads only when the stores go through a pointer local to the members (`uint32_t *rect = &field_58C_;`): VC6 caches member loads across direct same-base member stores and across anonymous-union array-member stores (both compile to the 80-byte no-reload form), but pointer-local stores invalidate that cache and produce the image's 98-byte form with all four call operands reloaded. With plain sums the pointer spelling also matches the image's load order, register assignment (y,x,height,width into eax,edx,esi,edi), folded direct stores and reload block byte-exactly; it is now the spelling at all eight rect sites in src/flic.cpp.
